title: Tech Note: Detecting the Presence of Externals in a 4D Database
author: Julie Pearson (revised by Jeff Browning)

historical_commentary.text: This note presents a clever workaround — deliberately triggering and trapping a syntax error via ON ERR CALL to detect whether an external/plugin such as 4D Write is installed — which was necessary because 4D lacked a built-in command to directly query plugin availability; the specific old/new external-architecture distinction (Mac4DX/Win4DX folders vs. pre-1.5 externals) is obsolete, but the general error-trapping technique remains conceptually recognizable, even though modern 4D plugin management and ORDA-era architecture make it largely unnecessary.
related_updates: 4D's plugin/component architecture has been substantially modernized since (4D Plugin SDK evolutions, and later Components/ORDA-based extension mechanisms), reducing the need for this error-trapping detection trick
4D Write itself was superseded by 4D Write Pro, introduced in 4D v14 (2016)
Modern 4D provides more direct ways to enumerate installed plugins/components rather than relying on deliberately causing and trapping a syntax error
